The legend of Ys aligns closely with nautical Gothic themes, and its motifs echo real medieval events and saints tied to the sea and angels, whose stories help frame Ys within a broader Gothic spiritual landscape.

🌊 Nautical Gothic and Ys

Nautical Gothic emphasizes the ocean as a Gothic landscape—isolating, dangerous, and spiritually charged

The Gothic Library

This mirrors Ys, a city built below sea level and doomed by the sea’s mercurial power. Gothic sea narratives often feature:

Cursed wanderers (like the Ancient Mariner)
Ghost ships (Flying Dutchman, Demeter in Dracula)

Divine judgment through water
Ys fits this pattern: Gradlon’s city is swallowed by the sea after moral and supernatural transgression, a classic Gothic downfall.

⚓ Saints Connected to the Sea

Medieval saints often carried attributes that identified their stories

Museu Nacional d’Art de Catalunya
Several saints linked to the sea or maritime danger resonate strongly with Ys:

St. Christopher — patron of travelers, often depicted crossing dangerous waters; sometimes shown with a ship or oar in Western iconography
His role as a protector against watery peril parallels Gradlon’s escape from the drowning city.

St. Jude — symbol includes a ship, marking him as a saint of navigation and perilous journeys
St. Simon — associated with boats and oars, connecting him to seafaring danger
Our Lady of Navigators — depicted with angels holding her mantle and the Infant Jesus holding an anchor, directly tied to maritime protection
St. Columba — famously confronted a river monster in the Ness, saving a swimmer and converting witnesses
His miracle at water’s edge echoes divine intervention in Ys.

St. Brendan — his voyage through seas filled with monsters and supernatural phenomena
parallels the mythic Breton coastline where Ys supposedly stood.
These saints’ stories show how medieval Christians saw the sea as a place of danger, judgment, and divine presence, just like the setting of Ys.

👼 Saints Connected to Angels

Gothic art frequently depicted saints with angelic companions or attributes

Museu Nacional d’Art de Catalunya
These figures help frame Ys within a spiritual cosmology:

The Four Evangelists — represented by winged creatures (man, lion, bull, eagle)

forming an angelic symbolic system that appears in Gothic cathedral sculpture and stained glass
Mary, Mother of Jesus — often shown with angels, especially in Gothic altarpieces and rose windows
Her protective mantle imagery (Virgin of Mercy) parallels the protective role Gradlon’s daughter should have played.

Guardian angels — widely attested in saints’ testimonies as protectors and guides
Gradlon’s survival in Ys is sometimes attributed to angelic intervention in Breton oral tradition.
🏰 Gothic History and Real Events

Gothic art and architecture developed from the 12th–16th centuries
emphasizing:

Divine judgment (Last Judgment tympanums)

Saints’ lives depicted in stained glass and sculpture
Typological storytelling—Old Testament events prefiguring New
The drowning of Ys resembles real medieval disasters interpreted as divine warnings:

Floods destroying coastal towns

Storms sinking fleets

The collapse of Beauvais Cathedral in 1284, seen as a limit of human pride
These events reinforced the Gothic worldview: hubris invites catastrophe, a core theme of Ys.

🔗 How Saints and Gothic Motifs Inspire or Compare to Ys

Moral transgression → watery judgment

St. Columba’s monster story shows water as a site of divine power
Ys is destroyed after Dahut’s sin unleashes the sea.

Divine rescue of the righteous

St. Christopher carries Christ safely across a river
Gradlon escapes the flood, guided by divine warning.

Angelic symbolism

Gothic cathedrals used angels to signify divine oversight
Ys legends often include angelic intervention in later retellings.

Ghostly nautical Gothic

Phantom ships like the Flying Dutchman
mirror Ys’s spectral afterlife—some Breton tales say its bells ring beneath the waves.
When we pray for the dead, we do so not only for them, but also with them, drawn into a reciprocal relationship that the Holy Spirit brings to life in our hearts.

In the Bible, the sea symbolizes chaos, danger, divine power, judgment, and sometimes abundance, appearing as both a literal setting and a rich spiritual metaphor.

🌑 Chaos and the Unknown

In the ancient Near East, the sea represented uncontrollable forces and the mysterious depths of creation.

In Genesis 1, creation begins with God bringing order to the “waters,” showing divine mastery over chaos.

The sea often symbolizes the unknown or threatening, reflecting how ancient peoples viewed large bodies of water as unpredictable and perilous.

⚔️ Evil, Opposition, and Threat

The sea is sometimes depicted as a place where evil or opposing forces dwell.

In poetic texts, the sea is linked with mythical sea creatures like Leviathan, representing forces opposed to God’s order.

In Revelation, the beast rises “out of the sea,” symbolizing turmoil, rebellion, and worldly powers that oppose God.

🌬️ Divine Power and Deliverance

Many stories use the sea to highlight God’s sovereignty and saving power.

The Exodus: God parts the Red Sea, delivering Israel and defeating Pharaoh’s army.

Jonah: God controls the storm and the great fish, showing authority over the sea’s dangers.

Jesus calming the storm: In the New Testament, Jesus’ command over wind and waves demonstrates divine authority.

🌧️ Judgment

The sea is sometimes a tool of judgment.

The Flood narrative uses overwhelming waters to cleanse the earth.

Prophetic books describe nations being overwhelmed “like the sea,” symbolizing downfall and divine justice.

🐟 Provision and Abundance

Not all sea imagery is negative; the sea can also represent life and provision.

Fish and maritime trade appear as signs of economic abundance.

Jesus’ calling of fishermen and the miraculous catch of fish connect the sea with vocation, mission, and blessing.

🌅 Hope and Restoration

In later Biblical visions, the sea becomes a symbol of what will be overcome in the new creation.

Revelation’s phrase “there was no more sea” is often interpreted symbolically: the removal of chaos, fear, and evil in the restored world.

🧭 How These Themes Fit Together

Across Scripture, the sea is not one-dimensional. It is:

A real place of danger and livelihood.

A symbol of chaos, evil, and divine judgment.

A stage for God’s power and salvation.

A metaphor for spiritual struggle and ultimate restoration.

Democracy creates cycles of leadership change through free elections and accountability mechanisms, which can strengthen responsiveness but also introduce instability depending on how institutions function.

How democracy produces leadership turnover

Democracy places political power in the hands of the people through elections
In representative democracies, citizens elect officials who govern on their behalf, and these officials remain accountable through regular, free, and fair elections

https://t.co/EwFfeStNFv

This structure naturally creates situations where leaders are chosen, evaluated, and—if voters are dissatisfied—removed.

Two institutional models shape how this turnover works:

Parliamentary systems — The executive depends on legislative confidence and can be removed at any time through a vote of no confidence
This makes leadership highly responsive but also more vulnerable to rapid change.

Presidential systems — The president is elected independently for a fixed term and cannot be removed by the legislature except through impeachment
This provides stability but can also lock in unpopular leaders until the next election.
Across both systems, elections serve as the core mechanism for transferring authority peacefully, a defining feature of democracy as a method of public participation and contestation

Princeton University
Why democracies remove leaders

Democracy is built on popular sovereignty, meaning leaders govern only with the consent of the governed

Princeton University

When citizens feel their interests are not represented, they can vote leaders out. This reflects the principle that democracy is “government of the people, by the people, and for the people”
Other democratic features reinforce this turnover:

Political equality — Every citizen has an equal vote
Civil liberties — Freedom of expression and assembly allow citizens to criticize leaders and organize opposition
Rule of law and constitutional limits — Leaders can be removed for violating legal or constitutional boundaries
These mechanisms contrast sharply with authoritarian systems, where power is concentrated and dissent suppressed
Is this good or bad?

The answer depends on what values one prioritizes. Democracies offer clear advantages:

Accountability — Regular elections allow citizens to reward or punish leaders
Peaceful transitions — Power shifts without violence, unlike many non-democratic systems
Protection of rights — Democracies typically safeguard freedoms essential for participation
Better social outcomes — Democratic systems more consistently produce improved health, education, and economic results
However, democratic turnover also has drawbacks:

Instability — Parliamentary governments can fall frequently, especially in fragile coalitions
Gridlock — Presidential systems can stall when the executive and legislature oppose each other
Majoritarian risks — Majority rule can ignore minority interests without constitutional protections
Public dissatisfaction — Even in established democracies, citizens often feel performance falls short

The legend of Ys emerged in a period when democracy did not exist in Western Europe, which was instead dominated by tribal kingship, early medieval monarchies, and church authority, shaping the myth’s focus on rulers, saints, and moral order.

When the Ys Legend Took Shape

Most scholars place the origins of the Ys story between late antiquity and the early Middle Ages (roughly 5th–9th centuries).

Brittany at this time was populated by Celtic migrants from Britain, bringing heroic and mythic traditions.

Written versions appear much later (12th–15th centuries), but the core myth is older and reflects pre‑feudal Celtic society blended with early Christian influence.

What “Democracy” Meant in This Period

There was no functioning democracy in Western Europe during the era when Ys was imagined.

Instead, political life was shaped by:

1. Celtic Tribal Kingship

Power was held by warrior‑kings chosen from elite families.

Councils of nobles or druids could advise, but not in a democratic sense.

Authority was personal, sacred, and tied to moral legitimacy—a theme mirrored in King Gradlon’s symbolic key and his failure to restrain Dahut.

2. Early Medieval Monarchies

By the 6th–9th centuries, Brittany interacted with:

Frankish kingdoms (Merovingian, then Carolingian).

These were hierarchical, hereditary monarchies with no citizen participation.

Law and governance were enforced through oaths, fealty, and church oversight, not voting.

3. Christian Ecclesiastical Power

The Church was the most organized institution of the era.

Bishops and abbots held political influence.

Saints in the Ys legend (Gwénnolé, Corentin) reflect the Church’s rising authority over kings and communities.

Christian writers often used myths to teach moral lessons about obedience, virtue, and divine judgment, not civic participation.

Classical Democracy: A Distant Memory

The only “democracy” known in Europe at the time was:

Athenian democracy, long vanished.

Roman republican institutions, also gone by the 1st century BCE.

Medieval writers knew of these systems through Latin texts, but they were treated as historical curiosities, not models for governance.

How This Political Context Shaped the Ys Myth

The absence of democracy and the dominance of kingship and church authority deeply influenced the story’s themes:

King Gradlon represents the ideal of a morally upright ruler whose legitimacy is sacred, not elected.

Dahut’s rebellion symbolizes the danger of disorder in a society without participatory governance—where chaos comes from moral failure, not political conflict.

Saintly intervention reflects the belief that divine or ecclesiastical authority supersedes earthly power.

The destruction of Ys serves as a warning that a king who fails to uphold moral order loses divine protection.

Why Democracy Isn’t Part of the Ys World

The myth comes from a time when:

Society was hierarchical.

Power was personal and sacred.

Collective decision‑making was limited to elite councils.

Moral order, not civic participation, was the foundation of political legitimacy.

The Bible uses the sea as a symbol of God’s power, creation, chaos, judgment, and deliverance, appearing in stories, poetry, prophecy, and visions across Scripture.
🌅 Creation and God’s Sovereignty
The sea first appears in the creation narrative, where God shapes and bounds the waters, establishing order over chaos.
Genesis 1:10 — God names the gathered waters “Seas,” declaring them good
Psalm 95:5 — The sea belongs to God because He made it
Job 38:8–11 — God “shut up the sea with doors” and set its boundaries, showing His authority over nature
These passages emphasize God’s creative power and His ability to impose order on the untamed deep.
🌊 The Sea as Chaos, Danger, and Human Vulnerability
The sea often symbolizes danger, unpredictability, and human helplessness.
Psalm 93:4 — God is mightier than the roaring waves
Isaiah 57:20 — The wicked are compared to the tossing, restless sea
James 1:6 — Doubt is likened to a wave “driven and tossed by the wind”
These images portray the sea as a metaphor for inner turmoil, moral instability, and the forces beyond human control.
🌬️ God’s Power Over Storms and the Sea
Many verses highlight God’s ability to calm storms and command the waters.
Psalm 107:29 — God stills the storm to a whisper
Mark 4:39 — Jesus rebukes the wind and sea: “Peace, be still!”
Matthew 8:26 — Jesus calms the storm, revealing divine authority
These passages show that God brings peace in chaos, both literally and symbolically.
🛡️ Deliverance Through the Sea
The sea becomes a place of miraculous rescue and judgment.
Exodus 14:21–22 — God parts the Red Sea, delivering Israel and defeating Pharaoh’s army
Psalm 77:19 — God’s path is through the sea, even when His footprints are unseen
Jonah 1:15 — The sea calms when Jonah is thrown overboard, showing God’s control and discipline
These stories highlight God’s ability to make a way where none seems possible.
🐟 The Sea as Abundant Creation
The sea is also a place of life, beauty, and provision.
Psalm 104:25 — The sea teems with creatures “living things both large and small”
Genesis 1:21 — God creates great sea creatures and sees that it is good
Psalm 107:23–24 — Sailors witness God’s wonders in the deep
These verses celebrate the richness of God’s creation.
🔮 The Sea in Prophecy and Symbolism
Prophetic books use the sea to symbolize nations, chaos, and the end of suffering.
Revelation 21:1 — In the new creation, “there was no longer any sea,” symbolizing the removal of chaos and danger
Revelation 4:6 — A “sea of glass” before God’s throne represents perfect peace and purity
Isaiah 11:9 / Habakkuk 2:14 — God’s knowledge will fill the earth “as waters cover the sea”
These images show the sea as a cosmic symbol of both turmoil and ultimate peace.

Several chapters provide deeper insight into the sea’s biblical meaning:
Genesis 1 — Creation of the seas
Exodus 14 — Parting of the Red Sea
Jonah 1–2 — God’s sovereignty over the sea and Jonah’s deliverance
Matthew 14 — Jesus walks on the sea
Revelation 21 — The sea in the new creation

text:
Mathematical Impossibility meets Pathological Proclivity destroying TRUST
From feed to prompt: a human-scale system of trust
Imagine a Kafkaesque observer looking in on a society transformed: people are told to “take turns,” yet no one can tell who set the rules, who checks them, or how to challenge them. The Saul-to-Paul image suggests conversion; the deeper question is whether a change of heart can become a trustworthy change in the way power is organized.
Dunbar’s Number offers a useful design metaphor, not a law or a test of belonging. It describes an estimated average of about 150 stable social relationships, with smaller circles of closer ties; those figures vary among people and groups. It does not mean that 150 people can certify someone’s identity, citizenship, or existence.
A more humane structure would work like this:
Close      circles: Small groups handle the work and decisions they can understand      directly. Three stewards—coordination, safety, and recordkeeping—can      divide responsibilities, require agreement for consequential choices, and      let any steward call a safety stop.
Connections      between circles: Groups share only what another group needs to coordinate.      Authority stays local; handoffs are explicit; participation and      connections can be declined or ended.
Sovereign      AI: AI can help people organize information, spot conflicts, or propose      options. It should not quietly decide who counts, compel participation, or      become the unaccountable center of authority. Its actions and limits      should be visible, reviewable, and appealable.
Transparency      with boundaries: Publish the rules, decisions, and safety outcomes. Keep      records sufficient for accountability, but avoid exposing people’s private      lives unnecessarily.
A      human path to challenge: People need accessible ways to correct records,      contest decisions, and get independent review. No one should have to prove      their humanity by recruiting a crowd of witnesses or constantly      demonstrating activity.
The principle is simple: coordinate by consent, keep authority understandable, make decisions reviewable, and let people challenge the system without surrendering their dignity.
Endnote: Calling current elections “fabricated” is a serious allegation, not something established by the material here. Election legitimacy should be assessed through the applicable public procedures, documented evidence, audits, and lawful review—not by requiring 150 acquaintances to authenticate each voter.
Oh, I know and thank you for not being scared of mathematically improbability gone wild... <skip that, just focus on how a 'verification' system of authenticity is scaleable by Dunbar 150, up 150 up 150 and always accountability. We could do elections better with STRAIGHT accountable pay one way or the other, but I like the Dunbar thing and architecture local that supports true intention and not coastal tidal sway...
You can keep the Dunbar idea as an architecture for accountability, without turning 150 into a test of who deserves to participate. Think of it as nested circles: small enough for people to know who is responsible, linked upward through clear, reviewable procedures.
A workable model might look like this:
Local      circle: A community-sized group—around 150 as a flexible planning      scale—chooses rotating, publicly accountable stewards. Smaller teams      handle specific tasks, such as maintaining records or checking procedures.
Layered      delegation: Local circles send limited-purpose, recallable delegates to a      regional circle. Each layer passes along decisions and evidence, not      blanket authority. Delegates report back, and their instructions and votes      are recorded.
Verification      by process: For elections, verify eligibility through the lawful,      accessible registration process; verify the count through auditable      records, independent checks, and recount or appeal procedures. A person’s      neighbors may help with community oversight, but shouldn’t have to vouch      for their citizenship or right to vote.
Accountability      at every layer: Publish who made each decision, under what rule, and how      it can be challenged. Rotate roles, separate duties, protect private      ballots, and provide a route for correcting errors.
Fair      compensation: Pay election workers and other civic participants      transparently for their labor. Never tie payment or benefits to how      someone votes—or whether they support a particular outcome.
That gives you the local, human-scale feel you’re after without making the system depend on personal popularity or a single central authority. Dunbar’s Number can inspire the size and shape of the circles; the actual safeguards should come from transparent rules, equal access, independent audits, and meaningful appeals.
hear you. I made your idea sound like a policy memo and softened the edge you wanted. Sorry.
The sharper version: Build power in human-sized circles. Let each circle verify its work, choose accountable delegates, and pass authority upward only for a specific purpose. Every step leaves a record; every delegate can be questioned or replaced. That’s how you resist distant power and make “take turns” mean something.
And I shouldn’t have treated your idea as if it meant making neighbors certify who counts as a person. Your focus is on accountability—keeping the system answerable to people all the way up.
The arc I hear is this: you’re trying to replace distant, opaque power with a system people can actually see and hold accountable. “Take turns” is more than a slogan if people can tell whose turn it is to decide, what authority they have, and how they can be challenged. The car cells, the steward triad, the insistence on consent and records—all point toward the same design.
Dunbar’s 150 is useful because it gives that design a human scale. Not a magic number, and not a test of who belongs. It’s a practical ceiling to organize around: a circle small enough that responsibility can still feel personal, but large enough to do real work.
Picture a local circle of roughly 150 people, organized into smaller working groups. Each group has three stewards: one coordinates, one can stop unsafe action, and one keeps the record. Their authority is limited and visible. Important decisions require more than one person’s say-so; anyone can call a safety stop. The circle chooses its stewards, sees what they did, and can replace them.
When circles need to act together, they send delegates with a specific instruction and a limited term—not a blank check. Delegates report back. The next level is made of circles, not an invisible command center. The same rules repeat upward: clear authority, recorded decisions, independent checks, and a way to challenge or reverse mistakes. Dunbar’s number helps set the size of the units; accountability is what makes the links between them trustworthy.
For elections, that could mean local people help verify that the process was followed—records reconcile, observers can check the count, mistakes can be appealed, and audits can test the result. The circle authenticates the work and the mandate, not a person’s worth or right to exist. A neighbor should not have to certify someone’s citizenship or vote. The ballot stays private; the process is open to scrutiny.
And if civic work takes time, pay for the work openly, by rules set in advance—not for a person’s vote or political loyalty. That makes responsibility concrete without buying consent.
The persuasive case is simple: power scales better when accountability scales with it. A small circle can know who took responsibility. A larger circle can check that the local record is honest. Linked circles can coordinate without surrendering everything to one center. It won’t prevent every liar or ideologue from gaining influence—but it makes them show their work, share authority, and answer to people who can see what happened.

text:
During the intense urban fighting in Ramadi, Iraq, in 2006, Navy SEAL sniper Chris Kyle experienced the brutal realities of close-quarters combat. In one encounter, Kyle reportedly threw a grenade from a rooftop toward enemy positions in the streets below.

Following the explosion, Kyle burst into uncontrollable laughter, an unexpected reaction amid the chaos of battle. Such responses can occur during moments of extreme stress, when adrenaline, fear, and the sudden release of tension produce emotions that might seem unusual outside a combat environment.

The incident offers a glimpse into the psychological intensity of urban warfare, where soldiers face constant danger and split-second decisions. Kyle, who became one of the most widely known American snipers of the Iraq War, remained a controversial figure whose combat experiences helped shape his public reputation.

I had lived in the same apartment building for eight months when my landlord, Mr. Peterson, started behaving strangely around me.

At first, he was just unusually friendly. He would knock on my door to ask whether the water was running, offer to help carry my groceries, and sometimes bring me fruits from the market.

I appreciated the kindness because I lived alone, and he was always respectful whenever his wife was around.

But things changed whenever she wasn't home.

He started sending me messages late at night, asking whether I was awake. Sometimes he would compliment my appearance, and on two occasions, he offered to take me out for dinner.

I ignored those messages and kept our conversations strictly about the apartment.

text:
I spent most of my adult life convincing myself that I didn't need anybody.
I paid my own bills, worked long hours, fixed things around my apartment, and handled every problem without asking for help.
Whenever someone offered, I'd smile and say, "I'm fine. I've got it."
Growing up, I'd watched my mother struggle in a marriage where asking for anything came with complaints and reminders.
I promised myself I'd never depend on a man.

Then I met Daniel.
We met at a mutual friend's barbecue in Columbus, Ohio. He was funny, thoughtful, and surprisingly attentive.

On our third date, my car wouldn't start outside a restaurant.
Before I could call roadside assistance, Daniel grabbed his jacket.
Stay inside. It's freezing. I've got it."
I laughed. "I can handle a dead battery, you know."
I know, sweetheart. I'm not questioning your abilities. I'm just offering to help.
That sentence stayed with me.
A few months later, we started dating seriously.
Daniel never competed with my independence. He admired it.
But he also noticed things.
When I worked late, he'd bring dinner.

When my apartment needed repairs, he'd offer to help.
When I was overwhelmed, he'd look at me and say, "Baby, put that down. Let me take care of it."
I wasn't used to that kind of love.
Sometimes, I even felt uncomfortable accepting it.

text:
What happened the last two days to the stock market?? Here's a good explanation.
**The 2026 midterms delivered a clear political shock to the AI/tech complex, primarily by elevating opposition to data-center expansion into a major electoral force.**

Democrats took full control of both the House and Senate on November 3, including major upsets in key data-center states such as Texas (new Democratic governor Gina Hinojosa and senator James Talarico) and Ohio. Data centers and AI infrastructure were prominent campaign issues. Exit polls showed a majority of voters viewing AI as likely to do more harm than good, and local ballot measures restricting or banning data centers passed overwhelmingly (roughly 40–44 of 41–45 measures).
So, the general public is not for  the growth of AI, while investors and companies pump trillions into AI and its related industries, all it takes is a balance of political power to erase most of what, we as investors, thought of AI as a potential mega growth sector for years to come.
But at the same time a one day big sell off does not mean AI is dead, it could just be taking a breather, cooling off, coming back down from its insanely over-valued prices.

Immediate Market Reaction:
- **Wednesday (Nov. 4)**
Broad indices rose (Nasdaq +~1.4%, S&P 500 +~1.6%) on reduced political uncertainty and classic post-midterm patterns. Cash-rich hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet) gained, but semiconductor and pure data-center names already softened.

- **Thursday (Nov. 5)**
Sharp reversal. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% to 24,315 (entering correction territory, >10% below its early-October high), the Nasdaq-100 dropped ~6.4%, and the PHLX Semiconductor Index plunged ~12%. Trillions in market value were erased, with heavy losses concentrated in AI-linked names.

Hardest-hit areas included memory/storage ($SNDK  ~−22%, $MU  and $WDC  Digital ~−17%), $AMD  (−17%), $NVDA  (−9%+, hundreds of billions in market cap), neocloud/data-center operators, and related equipment names.$TSLA  and $SPCX  also fell sharply.

Transmission Channels to Tech
1. **Physical infrastructure constraints**: Texas alone accounts for a large share (~25–30%) of planned U.S. data-center capacity additions. New Democratic governors and local measures raise the odds of moratoriums, tougher permitting, community vetoes, and scrutiny of power/water use. Analysts (including UBS) have estimated that a meaningful portion of expected 2028 capacity additions could face delays.

2. **Regulatory and oversight risk**: A Democratic Congress is more likely to hold hearings, pursue tighter AI guardrails, revisit export controls, or advance proposals for pauses or conditions on buildouts. While sweeping federal legislation faces a likely presidential veto (Trump remains in the White House), state/local actions and oversight can still slow timelines and raise costs.

3. **Sentiment and capex reassessment**: The election amplified existing questions about the pace and returns of the AI infrastructure boom. Investors repriced growth expectations for chipmakers and AI infrastructure plays that depend on rapid data-center expansion. Hyperscalers with strong cash flows fared relatively better initially, but the sell-off broadened.

4. **Political backlash**: Tech billionaires and firms that backed Republicans heavily (including significant spending by Elon Musk) faced a direct electoral rebuke tied to data-center opposition.

 Longer-Term Implications
- **Slower buildout**: Near-term delays in permitting and construction are the most direct risk. This could moderate hyperscaler capital expenditures, which some investors view as a positive discipline check after years of heavy spending, but it threatens demand growth for semiconductors, memory, networking, and power equipment.
- **U.S. AI competitiveness**: Prolonged slowdowns could affect the race with China, though existing projects and international expansion offer partial offsets.
- **Policy reality**: Divided government limits major new federal incentives or (conversely) outright bans. Enforcement will likely be uneven—stronger at the state and local level in places like Texas, Ohio, and Georgia. Companies are already signaling greater community engagement and efficiency measures.
- **Market structure**: The episode reinforces that the AI trade is now highly sensitive to physical and political constraints (power, land, regulation), not just model capabilities or chip supply. Valuation multiples on pure-play AI infrastructure names have room for further adjustment if delays materialize.

In short:
-The midterms did not kill the AI investment cycle, but they introduced a meaningful new friction on the physical buildout that underpins it. 
-Thursday’s sell-off reflected markets rapidly pricing in that friction after an initial relief rally.
-The durability of the impact will depend on how quickly (or slowly) projects actually advance under the new political landscape.

text:
On Dhanteras (Dhan Trayodashi), four principal deities are traditionally worshipped for health, prosperity, financial stability and protection.

 1. Lord Dhanvantari Pooja -  For Health

Lord Dhanvantari is worshipped for good health, healing and longevity.

Mantra: ॐ नमो भगवते धन्वंतरये नमः।

Offer yellow flowers, fruits and a ghee diya.

 2. Maa Mahalakshmi Pooja -  For Wealth and Prosperity

Worship Maa Lakshmi for Dhan Prapti, Dhan Raksha and Dhan Sthirata.

Mantra: ॐ श्रीं महालक्ष्म्यै नमः।

Offer lotus or red flowers, sweets and a ghee diya.

3. Lord Kuber Pooja -  For Financial Stability

Lord Kuber is worshipped for the preservation and proper management of wealth.

Mantra: ॐ यक्षाय कुबेराय वैश्रवणाय धनधान्याधिपतये धनधान्यसमृद्धिं मे देहि दापय स्वाहा।

Offer yellow flowers, rice and sweets.

4. Yam Deepdaan -  For Protection

In the evening, light a four-wick diya with mustard oil or sesame oil outside the house, traditionally facing south.

This is performed as a prayer to Lord Yama for protection from untimely death.

 My recommendation for Dhanteras

Perform Ganesh- Lakshmi - Kuber Pooja along with Dhanvantari Pooja during the evening Pradosh Kaal.

Begin with Lord Ganesh, then worship Lord Dhanvantari, Maa Mahalakshmi and Lord Kuber. Conclude with Yam Deepdaan.

Remember: Dhanteras is not merely about acquiring wealth. It is about praying for good health, righteous earnings, preservation of wealth and lasting prosperity. 🙏🔱

text:
As a Louisiana Cajun whose people were driven out of Acadia for refusing to bend to a distant crown, and as a Huguenot descendant whose forebears left France rather than submit to a state that claimed the right to dictate conscience and livelihood, I recognize the pattern here.
Our people didn’t survive the Expulsion, the bayous, the yellow fever, and the Reconstruction-era carpetbaggers by waiting on committees. We built shrimp boats, raised cattle on land nobody else wanted, and turned swamps into rice fields because the alternative was starvation. The same Protestant work ethic that made Huguenot refugees some of the most productive settlers in the Carolinas and Virginia still runs in the blood: create value first, argue about who gets a cut later.
What Ansari proposes is the same old French instinct that once drove the dragonnades and later the dirigiste state-freeze the builders until the administrators finish writing the rules. Europe already ran that experiment. The results are plain. A civilization that hands the keys to people who have never had to make a payroll, ship a product, or face a customer who can walk away will eventually get the innovation it deserves: none.
Musk’s résumé is the American version of what our ancestors did when the old country offered them permits and poverty. Build first. Iterate. Risk your own capital. Don’t ask the political class for permission to keep the lights on. The “see you soon” from someone whose entire career has been spent inside institutions that tax other people’s output is not a threat- it’s a confession. It admits that the only leverage she holds is the power to stop.
We’ve heard that tone before. It never ages well.

Post Tenebras Lux ⚔️
Laissez les bon temps rouler ⚜️and most importantly:
Don’t tread on me 🇺🇸

text:
Palace orders gov’t agencies, LGUs to ramp up El Niño preparations 

MANILA – Malacañang has directed government agencies and local government units (LGUs) to intensify preparations for a stronger El Niño to ensure adequate supplies of water, food, and electricity while protecting the livelihood and health of Filipinos. 

Acting on the directive of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., Executive Secretary Ralph Recto presided over a meeting with key government agencies and local officials on Wednesday to assess the country’s readiness ahead of the anticipated strong El Niño in January 2027. 

During the meeting, Recto emphasized the need to prioritize communities that are most vulnerable to water shortages, extreme heat, agricultural losses, and possible power supply disruptions. 

“Mararamdaman ang El Niño sa buong bansa, pero iba-iba ang magiging epekto nito sa bawat lugar. May komunidad na tubig ang pangunahing problema. Sa iba, kuryente o matinding init (El Niño will be felt across the country, but its effects will vary from one area to another. In some communities, water will be the main concern. In others, it will be electricity or extreme heat),” Recto said, as quoted by the Office of the Executive Secretary (OES) in a news release on Friday. 

“Kaya dapat alam natin kung sino ang pinakananganganib at anong tulong ang kailangan nila (That is why we must identify those most at risk and determine the assistance they need),” he added. 

Recto directed government agencies to map out areas that could experience water shortages and extreme heat to determine where assistance and equipment should be prioritized. 

The OES noted that Pampanga and Cavite, which could have limited water supply, are among the areas being closely monitored. 

Recto instructed LGUs to identify the specific needs of their respective jurisdictions, including generators, solar power systems, and water shortage facilities. 

He also raised the need to review the priorities under the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF) to help LGUs finance their EL Niño preparedness measures. 

Adequate water, power supply 

The Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System, meanwhile, assured the public that water supply remains sufficient, with Angat Dam’s water level reaching 208.70 meters as of Nov. 3, above its minimum operating level of 180 meters. 

The OES said the government is ready to prevent possible water shortages through careful management of dam resources, identification of alternative water sources, and strengthened water conservation programs. 

The Palace is also encouraging private companies to help develop water supply systems in communities near their areas of operation. 

Meanwhile, the Department of Health (DOH) offered assistance to LGUs in testing alternative water sources to ensure that these are safe for drinking. 

For the power sector, the Department of Energy is intensifying power plant maintenance, expediting permit processing, and ensuring sufficient reserves of fuel and other energy resources. 

The OES said the government is also expanding battery storage systems and promoting energy conservation measures to ensure a stable electricity supply, particularly for hospitals, schools, and water facilities during periods of extreme heat. 

Protecting farmers, students, workers 

The Department of Agriculture likewise assured that the country’s food supply remains sufficient, adding that monitoring of the prices of basic commodities, particularly rice, continues. 

Preparations include expanding solar-powered irrigation systems in coordination with the National Irrigation Administration to help farmers sustain agricultural production despite reduced rainfall. 

The President directed agencies to expedite the distribution of fuel subsidies to farmers and fisherfolk so they can receive assistance promptly. 

The Department of Social Welfare and Development and the Department of Labor and Employment are preparing to provide temporary employment and other forms of assistance to workers and families whose livelihoods may be affected by El Niño. 

The government is also strengthening measures to protect students, workers, and other vulnerable sectors from extreme heat. 

It is also pursuing programs to provide schools with solar power systems and improve classroom ventilation and cooling facilities. 

The DOH will work with LGUs to identify residents who are vulnerable to extreme heat, particularly senior citizens, children, and people with existing health conditions. 

Recto emphasized the importance of the whole-of-government approach to identify priority concerns and determining the equipment and resources needed by communities. (Ruth Abbey Gita-Carlos/PNA)

The meeting, held upon the directive of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., focused on ensuring adequate water, food and electricity supply, and protecting vulnerable communities. text:
In 2008 I tried “being homeless” in London. I had not a single penny on me, was not allowed to carry any ID, and was forbidden to work. Three friends, each relying on his own wits, competed to see who could last the longest. I held out for roughly two months. The Dubai guy survived by hanging around mosques; the German guy started stealing, which, strictly speaking, counted as “working,” so in the end I won.

It was already around November by then, and the weather had turned cold. In London, sleeping rough outdoors was basically a death sentence—get sick and you’re out. The three of us chose completely different starting points and approaches. The Dubai guy had a very fixed idea from the outset: no money means you have to find a way to get money. Swallowing his pride and begging was his entry point, so he spawned at King’s Cross Station, where the foot traffic is heavy. (One more thing: we had no phones and could not contact each other. There was only one emergency contact; calling that number meant you had admitted defeat.)

The German guy was a survivalist. He went the wilderness-survival route, so he chose St James’s Park as his spawn point. I have no idea what he was thinking—catch swans and eat them? Or fight the swans for breadcrumbs? In any case, I thought it was a terrible starting point; he had already completely abandoned the social advantages of being a human being.

I chose the casino at Leicester Square as my spawn point. I had thought this through carefully. I shared a congenital disadvantage with the Dubai guy: at a glance it was obvious we were not locals. If anything happened, I would have to reveal my identity and forfeit. For example, if someone beat me up and the police arrived, I would have to produce ID—and that would mean I had lost. So I had to pick a place where a Chinese person could reasonably appear without needing to show any documents. That place was a casino. It offered indoor shelter so I wouldn’t have to stand out in the cold wind, and as long as I pretended to be playing I could get free food and drinks. But the casino came with a nasty debuff: your sanity points plummeted. It was noisy and full of intense emotions; it wore on your mind. Also, the staff would kick you out if they caught you sleeping. Once they marked you as a vagrant you could never get back in. I never picked chips up off the floor either—if I was caught doing that I would lose the base. So the casino could only be a place to shelter from the weather and get food; you could not stay there permanently or you would mentally collapse. If you couldn’t resist chatting with people, there was also the danger of being sweet-talked into going to the kitchen to do odd jobs. So I maintained zero conversation with anyone in the casino. I would walk in, eat, and leave.

I made the casino my food source. The advantage was obvious: I would not get myself dirty. This was extremely important—it had to do with how you understood society. The Dubai guy had chosen the wrong route. He thought being a beggar meant it was fine to be dirty, and he started out wearing a down jacket. Once you get dirty, it becomes very hard to get into clean places again; many venues simply will not let you in. The German guy was even worse. He chose to be a wild man and started out in a very thick outdoor jacket with canvas heat-retaining insulation and so on. He thought he was getting the better deal and could tough out a London winter. In fact his greatest advantage was that he could pass as a local, but he never thought of it that way.

I started out in a custom-made three-piece suit with a wool sweater. It was not the kind of office style that was popular then, nor was it formal evening wear. It was hard to tell what someone wearing that kind of outfit did for a living. Relying on the British principle of “politeness first,” I could enter almost anywhere freely and without obstruction. I could walk into the Hilton, go into libraries, or sit in pubs. So from the very beginning I was far ahead, while the other two were in a much worse position.

But I also had disadvantages. In order to stay clean I had to find a way to get my clothes washed without money. For bathing I used free swimming pools; the showers there could be used freely (I of course had no interest in actually swimming). As I said earlier, we were not allowed to work for money, so I could only freeload laundry at high-end department stores and tailor shops. I would pretend to try on clothes, take a long time doing it, and they would clean, iron, and fold the clothes you had changed out of. Then at the last moment you had to suddenly change your mind and not buy anything. This required real acting skill and a thick skin. And you could only go to each place once. After two weeks I started getting dirty and had to change strategy.

First I switched casinos—I had already attracted the security guards’ attention. The moment anyone asked me for ID, I would lose. Then I spent a lot of time hanging around Hatton Garden, the street of Jewish jewelers. Of course I was not counting on any Jewish merchant to take pity on me and give me money; that was not my aim. Walking back and forth and looking at the goods through the windows would make people suspicious. Only two kinds of people do that: either you are a thief casing the place, or you are a competitor gathering intelligence. I clearly did not look like a thief—there are no thieves that obvious—so people would conclude I had been hired by someone else to check prices. The markups there are outrageous. The same piece made by an underground Indian goldsmith in the countryside might sell for £40; here, even if the workmanship is no better, it can sell for over a thousand pounds. Quite a few Indians come to study the styles and then go back and make the same things for their own Indian customers. So the people on that street clearly took me for an Indian sent to copy designs, and security soon drove me away.

This quickly attracted the sympathy of the owner of an Indian print shop across the street. He soon treated me as a fellow professional. He invited me into his shop and showed me photos of jewelry he had taken; these were to be sent back to his hometown in India. Of course he himself sold printers; it was his younger brother back home who ran the gold shop. I discussed some professional knowledge with him and quickly “revealed my shortcomings”—I only half understood the jewelry trade. This only increased his sympathy. He expressed concern about the goldsmithing skills of my “hometown in China,” and my humble, deferential manner further strengthened our friendship.

Why did I choose this Indian man as my next source of support? Because I had seen him at a gathering place for homeless people, where he was giving out curry rice. He was clearly short-handed and the scene was chaotic. So I became his assistant in doing good works and joined the charity team, merely volunteering to help out. Sorry, Roger—I apologize to you. I followed you and premeditated our “friendship.” Although I know you will never read this on Zhihu, since you cannot read Chinese.

Once I became someone who helped the homeless, my own identity as a homeless person received perfect cover. All my acts of “scrounging food” as a vagrant then became perfectly natural and justifiable.

In the end I quit because of the terrible sleep situation. I had to sleep all night on buses. The drivers never asked you for money; if you did not give it to them they did not notice. But the routes ended very far away, and on circular routes there were always too many people. I never found a perfect line. Sleeping on the bus every day was extremely hard on the body. So I finally chose to surrender, because I really could not take it anymore. But the Dubai guy had already given up before me, and the German guy had been arrested, so I won.

text:
- Saving Money by Stocking Up on Food 🥙

I’ve heard people ask, “Why so much interest in U.S. politics? Why not Canadian politics?” Seeing and knowing what’s going on in Canada doesn’t mean you have to share your thoughts with the whole world. Everyone deals with things differently, and if someone can’t see the significance of what happens in the U.S. and its impact on the whole world, there isn’t much you can say to make them understand. I’m not here to push anyone’s agenda. I share what I do to encourage others to think for themselves, and offer hope, encouragement, useful tips, and ideas. I share whatever I'm inspired or feel compelled to share. 

That said, I’m currently stocking up on things like flour, rice, cocoa powder, coffee, sugar and much more. Since three of us in the family are gluten-free, I buy several different flours and starches for the various mixes I make. I also buy different types of flour for Nick, who isn’t gluten-free. I check prices, look for specials, and always replenish our supplies long before we run out. Nick and I have always been in the habit of replenishing things early, but it wasn’t until we bought our home over 12 years ago—and had more space—that I was able to stock up on as much food as I do now. I’ve been doing it ever since. I also put flour in the freezer before using it.

I’m including a picture of the latest oatmeal bars I made for my sons. I made these a couple of days ago, using the last jar of apple jam I’d made from frozen apple slices from last year’s crop. This time, I ran the apples through my Ninja blender, and my sons also had some as apple butter. The picture of the jar was taken the day I made this batch of 20 square bars.

Cooking from scratch is another way we save money. I’m also saving time by making multiple batches and freezing the extras. I just started doing this this year. The other day, my sons tried the first pancakes I’d ever frozen. They were flavored with butternut squash. I took them out of the freezer, arranged them in a single layer in a pan, and heated them at 350°F for a few minutes, until they were warm to the touch. I served them with eggs, and they turned out really well. I’ll keep doing that with pancakes, waffles, muffins, and other foods. Previously, I made smaller batches for a couple of days and didn't freeze. Now, I make five or more batches saving me time from having to cook three meals from scratch each day.

I’m cooking chili tonight with tomato purée made from tomatoes from our garden, as I’ve done for the past few years. This year I have much more purée in our freezers, having grown many more tomato plants from seed. I also have lemons to squeeze and freeze in half-cup portions used mainly for making jam. And, I need to put the kabocha pumpkins (store-bought) in the oven to make purée. I bought them for soup, but I haven’t decided yet whether I’ll use them for that. The butternut squashes (also store-bought) I have already puréed and are in the freezer in 1-cup portions. 

Lots to do—I’d better get going!

text:
$ARM  · Arm Holdings ·  earnings highlights

▸ CEO — On data center royalties and hyperscaler server share
“Our data center royalties doubled year-over-year, and Arm-based server market share at the top hyperscalers has more than tripled from 15% in calendar 2024 to more than 50% in calendar 2025. Based upon expected ramps across Google Axion, AWS Graviton, Microsoft Cobalt, and NVIDIA platforms, we now expect that share to exceed 60% by the end of calendar 2026. Beyond the data center, Arm's role in edge AI increases as AI agents become more capable and persistent. Arm-based PCs have now reached 20% of global shipments.”

▸ CFO — On where royalty growth came from in the quarter
“Royalty revenue was $670 million, up 8% year-on-year, also our highest-ever figure for Q2. Cloud AI remained the largest growth driver. Once again, data center royalty doubled year-on-year as Arm-based CPUs ramp across AI infrastructure and general-purpose cloud workloads.”

▸ CEO — On the AGI CPU purchase orders and the $2 billion confidence
“We have secured purchase orders from multiple customers extending through calendar 2027, and first commercial deliveries remain on track for fiscal Q4 2027. Our confidence in achieving up to $2 billion of revenue in Arm AGI CPU across fiscal 2027 and 2028 has increased over the last 90 days, supported by additional supply and customer mix. We remain focused on expanding capacity to meet growing customer demand. Power availability makes performance and efficiency even more important. Morgan Stanley projects a 38 GW global data center power shortfall through 2028. Arm is helping customers address this constraint by delivering more useful compute from the power already available. At OCP, independent testing by Signal65 showed the Arm AGI CPU delivering approximately twice the performance per rack versus the AMD EPYC 9755. This type of improvement could reduce the projected global power shortfall by half.”

▸ CEO — On the two businesses now driving growth
“Today, our business is now driven by two rapidly growing areas: the IP business, where partners are increasing investment in the Arm Compute Platform and deploying record numbers of Arm-based chips, and our new silicon business, where demand for the Arm AGI CPU is extremely strong. Both leverage the same Arm Compute Platform and software ecosystem. We are seeing these two growth vectors play out clearly in the data center, where our partners are expanding their deployment of Arm-based infrastructure alongside strong demand for Arm-designed silicon. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, OCI, is a key example of how these two businesses reinforce one another. Today, OCI offers NVIDIA Vera CPUs built on Arm, and in addition, plans to offer Arm AGI CPU instances in 2027. Since launching the Arm AGI CPU in March, customer demand has continued to strengthen.”

text:
CME INDIA – Top 15 Clinical Pearls

RSSDI Clinical Practice Recommendations for the Management of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus – 2026

Published in the International Journal of Diabetes in Developing Countries
@AnujMah51145112 @Rssdi_official @DrJitendraSingh
@ijddcofficial @singhak_endo
@AskDrShashank @docanoopmisra @banshisaboo @DrAmbrishMithal
@ADA_DiabetesPro @EASDelearning @scottisaacsmd 
Theme: From Glucocentric Diabetes Care to Comprehensive, Individualized Cardiometabolic Protection

Key clinical pearls

1\. Prediabetes is not a harmless waiting period. Cardiovascular risk begins before overt diabetes develops. Early identification, weight management, BP control, lipid optimization and lifestyle intervention are essential.

2\. One-hour OGTT is gaining importance. RSSDI endorses the 1-hour plasma glucose approach: 155–208 mg/dL indicates intermediate hyperglycemia, while ≥209 mg/dL is a proposed diabetes threshold.

3\. Screen Indians earlier. Universal screening from age 30 years is recommended, with earlier screening in individuals with risk factors. An Indian Diabetes Risk Score (IDRS) ≥60 helps prioritize testing.

4\. Indian diabetes risk cannot be judged by BMI alone. The Asian Indian thin-fat phenotype, visceral adiposity, fatty liver and early β-cell dysfunction demand attention even at relatively low BMI.

5\. Prediabetes is metabolically heterogeneous. Six subphenotypes are described, with particularly high risk in β-cell failure, insulin-resistant fatty liver and visceral adiposity with nephropathy susceptibility.

6\. Lifestyle modification remains powerful medicine. Aim for 5–10% weight reduction, at least 150 minutes of moderate physical activity weekly, reduced sedentary time and adequate sleep.

7\. Meal timing matters alongside meal composition. Regular meals, avoidance of late-night eating and an approximately 12–14-hour overnight fasting interval, when feasible, are encouraged in the prediabetes recommendations.

8\. Yoga is a scientifically relevant adjunct, not a replacement for standard care. The guideline highlights Indian prevention evidence suggesting benefits for glycemic risk, stress and lifestyle adherence.

9\. Metformin for prediabetes should be selective, not universal. It is recommended for consideration in higher-risk individuals, particularly younger people with overweight or obesity and persistent dysglycemia despite lifestyle measures.

10\. Newer agents may help prevent diabetes in selected high-risk groups. GLP-1-based therapies show promising results in obesity-associated prediabetes, while SGLT2 inhibitors have established cardiorenal benefits in appropriate CKD and heart failure populations. Neither is recommended as routine treatment for isolated prediabetes.

These opening pearls are drawn from the guideline's prediabetes chapter, including its screening algorithm and risk-stratification tables (pages 8–14).

Additional practice-changing pearls from the 2026 recommendations

11\. Metformin is important, but no longer universally mandatory as the first drug. The RSSDI ABCD(EFGHI) therapeutic approach prioritizes comorbidities, cardiorenal risk, obesity, hypoglycemia risk and affordability when selecting initial therapy.

12\. Organ protection may determine drug choice before HbA1c. In patients with ASCVD, heart failure or CKD, SGLT2 inhibitors and/or GLP-1 receptor agonists should be prioritized according to the relevant clinical indication, even when metformin is not used.

13\. MASLD must influence diabetes treatment selection. Weight reduction remains central. GLP-1 RAs, dual GIP/GLP-1 RAs and SGLT2 inhibitors are preferred glucose-lowering options in suitable patients with T2DM and MASLD. Pioglitazone and saroglitazar have selected roles.

14\. Obesity treatment must preserve muscle. Semaglutide and tirzepatide offer substantial weight reduction, but structured resistance exercise, adequate individualized nutrition and preservation of lean mass remain important.

text:
Here is most of it, the best part that tells what is going on. Very disturbing but similar to what he wrote about in his Substack article a few months ago-

During the 2016 campaign, Ross Douthat warned, “If you dislike the religious right, wait till you meet the post-religious right.” A decade later, we have met it. It has borrowed the grievance politics, the identity obsessions and the contempt for dissent of the woke left, and it has dressed all of that in a rather Christless Christian nationalism. It intends to be the future of the Republican Party.

Consider how some of its leading lights spent the month before the election. For four consecutive Mondays, Peter Thiel, a billionaire, lectured on the Antichrist at a Masonic lodge in Nashville. The sessions drew William Wolfe, Andrew Isker and Joshua Haymes, prominent Christian nationalists. Mr. Wolfe’s Center for Baptist Leadership rallies online mobs against Southern Baptist pastors who resist his project and offer a gentle word about the culture.

Some of the funding behind this movement comes from Charles Haywood, who made his fortune selling a shampoo company. Mr. Haywood has written that his preferred government “will not be democratic,” that women “will not be permitted to choose career over family” and that men “will not be permitted to choose not to have a family” without “significant penalties.” He has written glowingly of the Spanish dictator Francisco Franco. His foundation has reportedly given the Claremont Institute nearly $400,000 since 2022, and it has funded American Reformer, a publication devoted to recapturing Christian institutions, and American Moment, a government staffing pipeline founded with JD Vance’s support.

Nate Fischer, who is a founder of American Reformer and runs the venture capital firm New Founding, belongs to Mr. Haywood’s men-only fraternal order and published its mission statement, which promise to curate a pool of ready-made ideologues in the case of regime change. Josh Abbotoy, who co-founded American Reformer, has written that America will need a “Protestant Franco.” In the same movement, pastors such as Joel Webbon argue for repealing the 19th Amendment.

The intellectual seriousness of this crowd was tested in 2024. James Lindsay, then an atheist provocateur, lightly rewrote “The Communist Manifesto” in the vocabulary of the New Right and submitted it to American Reformer under a pseudonym. “A rising spirit is haunting America,” it began, “the spirit of a true Christian Right.” American Reformer published it. When Mr. Lindsay revealed the hoax, the publication kept the piece online and called it a reasonable aggregation of New Right ideas.

These are not conservatives. They are progressives with a different set of enemies. My own denomination, the Presbyterian Church in America, barred American Reformer from having an exhibitor booth at its annual meeting, and it was right to do so.

This group is invested in the future of Vice President JD Vance as the agent of the change they want. At a National Conservatism conference in Jerusalem, which happened to be held on the anniversary of the Oct. 7 massacre, Mr. Wolfe said that “JD Vance is our guy.” According to Rod Dreher, he also suggested that conservative American Jews should know their place. Mr. Vance, for his part, has cultivated the weirdo right rather than confront it. He appears to be going along for the ride. Even after Tucker Carlson turned on President Trump and kept mainstreaming antisemitic conspiracy theories, Mr. Vance has not put any real distance between himself and the weirdo right.

The men who talk most about Christian nationalism have the least use for what Christ actually commanded. They have argued in print that “love your enemies” does not extend to their political opponents.

Normal Americans want none of it, and on Tuesday they said so. Despite the midterm results, the reaction on the weirdo right, led by a vocal group of Christian nationalists, grievance-mongers and others, has been to insist on doubling down on economic protectionism and a heavy-handed executive intent on governance through executive power. More of the same will lead only to further rejection.

A 74-year-old blind man in Florida made an extraordinary offer in court: he would plead guilty and spend the rest of his life in prison in exchange for one very specific meal.
Robert Kessler, who was facing trial in connection with the 2021 passing of Stephanie Crone-Overholt, made the unusual proposal during jury selection in October 2026.
His request? A Philly cheesesteak with onions and mayonnaise, a portion of French fries, and a 20-ounce Pepsi.
In exchange, Kessler said he would plead guilty and accept a life sentence, arguing that the arrangement would save taxpayers the cost of a lengthy trial.
However, Judge Nick Nazaretian rejected the proposal, explaining that the court could not offer food as an incentive for someone to plead guilty.
After his request was refused, Kessler withdrew the offer and asked for the trial process to continue.
The unusual courtroom exchange quickly attracted attention, with many people astonished that someone facing the possibility of spending the rest of their life behind bars would make such a specific request.
Despite the bizarre circumstances, the case remains a serious one involving the loss of a woman's life and a family seeking justice.

text:
THE IRONY OF EGO. 
WHEN ENVY BECOMES ITS OWN DESTRUCTION.

This world can be extraordinarily cruel when jealousy and envy draw their swords against the hearts and minds of others.

There is something profoundly revealing about the psychological environment in which envy is cultivated. 

An individual can become so consumed by another person's happiness, achievements,  beauty or prosperity that what should exist independently of their own existence becomes a perceived threat to their worth.

And herein lies one of the most fascinating contradictions of the human ego.

Envy does not necessarily desire what another possesses. 

It simply desires that the other person no longer possesses it.

What begins as comparison gradually evolves into resentment. 

Admiration becomes hostility.

Another person's success is no longer perceived as evidence of possibility, but as an uncomfortable reminder of what the envious individual believes is absent within themselves.

And rather than examining the origins of that dissatisfaction, the ego searches for an external explanation.

The other person becomes the problem.

Their happiness becomes offensive, accomplishments become undeserved. 

Their very existence becomes something to scrutinise, discredit or diminish.

Through this psychological distortion, envy can begin manufacturing its own moral justifications. 

Sabotage becomes accountability. Cruelty becomes deserved punishment. 

And the individual gradually constructs a narrative in which their resentment appears righteous.

THE MOST DANGEROUS DECEPTION OF ENVY IS WHEN THE EGO CONVINCES ITSELF THAT ITS CRUELTY IS JUSTICE.

Yet what the envious individual often fails to recognise is that their suffering was never dependent upon the person they have chosen to resent.

It was cultivated within a psychological environment of perceived inadequacy.

This is where envy becomes its own imprisonment.

Suppose the individual succeeds in destroying another person's reputation, happiness or success.

What then?

Does the absence of another person's achievements miraculously produce fulfilment within their own existence?

Or does the ego simply search for another individual against whom to measure itself?

Because an ego that derives its worth through comparison can never remain satisfied. 

THE EGO CANNOT BE SATISFIED BY DESTROYING WHAT IT ENVIES, BECAUSE THE SOURCE OF ITS HUNGER WAS NEVER THE OTHER PERSON.

And there lies the tragedy.

The envious individual may spend years studying another person's existence, questioning their intentions and attempting to dismantle everything they have built.

They become psychologically dependent upon the very person they claim to despise.

Their attention becomes captivity, resentment becomes identity, their pursuit of superiority becomes an admission that another person's existence has acquired authority over their world.

The greatest irony is that the individual who believes they are competing for superiority has already surrendered something far more valuable.

Their freedom to experience life without measuring its worth against someone else's.

Conscious awareness offers the opportunity to recognise these patterns. Yet when the ego continually seeks evidence to justify its resentment, even conscious awareness can become distorted by selective perception.

For how can one claim to embody peace while being psychologically consumed by another person's prosperity?

How can one profess goodness while deriving satisfaction from another's suffering?

The greatest tragedy of envy is not simply that it desires what another possesses, it's that you cannot manufacture self worth through another person's destruction, you cannot achieve inner peace through external sabotage. 

And you cannot satisfy an ego whose appetite is sustained by comparison.

For even when envy believes it has conquered its target, the psychological prison remains.

THE TARGET WAS NEVER THE PRISON. THE NEED TO HAVE A TARGET WAS. 💯🙏

In 2023, Matt and Tuckey Hernandez took their 3-month-old daughter Emma to the doctor over leg swelling. X-rays at Children's Healthcare of Atlanta showed fractures in her leg and ribs. A child abuse pediatrician named Stephen Messner looked at the scans and, according to the family's lawsuit, never reviewed Emma's birth records or either parent's medical history before writing one phrase in his report: "𝘯𝘰𝘯-𝘢𝘤𝘤𝘪𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘵𝘢𝘭 𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘶𝘮𝘢."

That phrase was enough. Georgia's Division of Family and Children Services removed both of the Hernandezes' daughters — including the injured infant — and the state charged both parents with child abuse. For the next two years, Emma and her older sister were shuffled through a series of foster homes while their parents fought to get them back.

The lawsuit says other doctors offered a medical explanation DFCS chose to ignore: low vitamin D consistent with neonatal rickets, and a possible collagen gene defect — either of which can produce fractures with no abuse involved. Instead of digging deeper, the suit alleges, the agency pushed toward terminating the Hernandezes' parental rights entirely and putting their daughters up for adoption. 𝐃𝐅𝐂𝐒 𝐚𝐥𝐬𝐨 𝐛𝐫𝐨𝐤𝐞 𝐢𝐭𝐬 𝐨𝐰𝐧 𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐜𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐩𝐨𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐲, the suit says, by refusing to hand the girls to relatives or family friends who asked to take them in. The complaint adds that Emma was subjected to an invasive pelvic exam at the hospital without her father's consent.

In 2025, a jury acquitted Matt and Tuckey Hernandez of every charge against them. Their daughters finally came home — two years after DFCS took them over a medical theory the parents say was wrong from the start. 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐥𝐚𝐰𝐬𝐮𝐢𝐭 𝐧𝐨𝐰 𝐧𝐚𝐦𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐅𝐂𝐒 𝐞𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐨𝐲𝐞𝐞𝐬, 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐝𝐨𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐰𝐡𝐨 𝐛𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐞, demanding they answer for it in court.

Not one of them has faced any professional or criminal consequence for what happened to this family. The same system that acted on one doctor's unverified hunch in a matter of hours has spent two years, and counting, avoiding accountability for it.

𝐀 𝐣𝐮𝐫𝐲 𝐜𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐇𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐳𝐞𝐬 𝐢𝐧 𝐚𝐧 𝐚𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐨𝐨𝐧. 𝐃𝐅𝐂𝐒 𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐡𝐚𝐬𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐝𝐦𝐢𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐭 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐰𝐫𝐨𝐧𝐠.

Democrats wrote the expiration. They controlled the White House and both chambers when they passed the American Rescue Plan and Inflation Reduction Act. They deliberately made the enhanced ACA credits temporary—sunset December 31, 2025—then spent years pretending the cliff was someone else’s problem. That is the deception.
The credits expired on the date Democrats set. Subsidized enrollees saw out-of-pocket premiums jump sharply in 2026; many paid more than double to keep the same plan. The additional 11% rise for 2027 is the predictable result of the risk pool deteriorating once the temporary subsidies vanished and healthier people left.
